questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: She writes a letter.

options.option_text: A letter was written by her.
A letter is written by her.
A letter is wrote by her.
A letter is being written by her.

questions.explanation: Simple present passive: is/am/are + V3. 'She writes' → 'A letter is written by her'. Past participle of 'write' is 'written', not 'wrote'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The cat caught the mouse.

options.option_text: The mouse is caught by the cat.
The mouse were caught by the cat.
The mouse was caught by the cat.
The mouse was being caught by the cat.

questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was/were + V3. Subject 'cat' is singular → 'was'. 'Caught' is past participle of 'catch'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: They are building a new bridge.

options.option_text: A new bridge was being built by them.
A new bridge is being built by them.
A new bridge has been built by them.
A new bridge is built by them.

questions.explanation: Present continuous passive: is/am/are + being + V3. 'Are building' → 'is being built'. The passive subject 'bridge' is singular, so 'is'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: He has solved the problem.

options.option_text: The problem was solved by him.
The problem had been solved by him.
The problem is solved by him.
The problem has been solved by him.

questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: has/have + been + V3. 'Has solved' → 'has been solved'. The passive subject 'problem' is singular, so 'has'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The teacher will explain the lesson.

options.option_text: The lesson is explained by the teacher.
The lesson would be explained by the teacher.
The lesson will be explained by the teacher.
The lesson will have been explained by the teacher.

questions.explanation: Simple future passive: will + be + V3. 'Will explain' → 'will be explained'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: She was cooking dinner.

options.option_text: Dinner is being cooked by her.
Dinner was cooked by her.
Dinner was being cooked by her.
Dinner had been cooked by her.

questions.explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were + being + V3. 'Was cooking' → 'was being cooked'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: Ram opened the door.

options.option_text: The door is opened by Ram.
The door was opened by Ram.
The door were opened by Ram.
The door has been opened by Ram.

questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was/were + V3. 'Opened' is both simple past and past participle. 'Door' is singular → 'was'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: He had completed the project.

options.option_text: The project was completed by him.
The project has been completed by him.
The project had been completed by him.
The project had completed by him.

questions.explanation: Past perfect passive: had + been + V3. 'Had completed' → 'had been completed'. The auxiliary 'been' is mandatory.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The mechanic will repair the car.

options.option_text: The car is repaired by the mechanic.
The car will repaired by the mechanic.
The car will be repaired by the mechanic.
The car will have been repaired by the mechanic.

questions.explanation: Simple future passive: will + be + V3. 'Will repair' → 'will be repaired'. 'Be' cannot be omitted.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: People know him well.

options.option_text: He was well known by people.
He is well known by people.
He is being well known by people.
He has been well known by people.

questions.explanation: Simple present passive: is + V3. 'People know him' → 'He is known by people'. Adverb 'well' is placed before the past participle.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: They elected him president.

options.option_text: He was elected as president by them.
He is elected president by them.
He was elected president by them.
He has been elected president by them.

questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was + V3. 'Him' becomes 'He'. 'President' is a predicative object and stays without 'as'. Tense: simple past → was elected.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: She bought a new dress.

options.option_text: A new dress is bought by her.
A new dress was bought by her.
A new dress has been bought by her.
A new dress was being bought by her.

questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was/were + V3. 'Bought' is past participle of 'buy'. 'She' → 'by her'. 'A new dress' becomes the subject.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: We have finished the work.

options.option_text: The work was finished by us.
The work is finished by us.
The work had been finished by us.
The work has been finished by us.

questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: has/have + been + V3. 'We have finished' → 'The work has been finished by us'. 'Work' is singular → 'has'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The dog bit the child.

options.option_text: The child is bitten by the dog.
The child was bit by the dog.
The child was bitten by the dog.
The child had been bitten by the dog.

questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was + V3. Past participle of 'bite' is 'bitten' (not 'bit'). 'Was bit' is nonstandard.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: My father planted these trees.

options.option_text: These trees are planted by my father.
These trees were planted by my father.
These trees had been planted by my father.
These trees were being planted by my father.

questions.explanation: Simple past passive: were + V3 (plural subject 'trees'). 'Planted' is past participle.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: Nobody can solve this puzzle.

options.option_text: This puzzle can't be solved by nobody.
This puzzle cannot be solved by anybody.
This puzzle could not be solved by anybody.
This puzzle cannot solve by anybody.

questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + V3. 'Nobody can solve' → 'cannot be solved by anybody'. 'Nobody' becomes 'anybody' in the by-phrase to avoid double negative.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change the following question to Passive Voice: Why did he write such a letter?

options.option_text: Why was such a letter written by him?
Why was such a letter write by him?
Why such a letter was written by him?
Why has such a letter been written by him?

questions.explanation: Passive of WH-question (simple past): Why + was/were + subject + V3 + by + agent? The question word 'Why' is retained at the front. Auxiliary 'was' is inverted.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Active: She gave him a book. Which passive sentence uses the INDIRECT object ('him') as the new subject?

options.option_text: A book was given to him by her.
He was given a book by her.
A book was given by her to him.
He was being given a book by her.

questions.explanation: With double-object verbs, either object can become the passive subject. When the indirect object 'him' becomes the subject: 'He was given a book by her'. No 'to' is needed before the direct object.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The police arrested fifty people.

options.option_text: Fifty people are arrested by the police.
Fifty people were being arrested by the police.
Fifty people had been arrested by the police.
Fifty people were arrested by the police.

questions.explanation: Simple past passive: were + V3 (plural subject 'fifty people'). 'Police' is the agent.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice (drop the agent): Someone had broken the window.

options.option_text: The window has been broken by someone.
The window was broken.
The window had been broken.
The window is broken.

questions.explanation: Past perfect passive: had + been + V3. When the agent is 'someone' (unknown), the by-phrase is omitted. 'Had broken' → 'had been broken'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The government has launched a new scheme.

options.option_text: A new scheme was launched by the government.
A new scheme has been launched by the government.
A new scheme had been launched by the government.
A new scheme is launched by the government.

questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: has + been + V3. 'Has launched' → 'has been launched'. 'Scheme' is singular → 'has'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice (imperative): Open the door.

options.option_text: The door must be opened.
Let the door be opened.
The door will be opened.
The door is to be opened.

questions.explanation: Passive of imperative: 'Let + object + be + V3'. 'Open the door' → 'Let the door be opened'. This is the standard exam-tested form.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice (causative): She makes him do the work.

options.option_text: He is made do the work by her.
He is made to do the work by her.
He was made to do the work by her.
He was made do the work by her.

questions.explanation: Causative 'make + object + bare infinitive' → passive: 'object + is/was + made + to + infinitive'. The bare infinitive gains 'to' in the passive.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The author will have written three books by December.

options.option_text: Three books will be written by the author by December.
Three books would have been written by the author by December.
Three books will have been written by the author by December.
Three books will have written by the author by December.

questions.explanation: Future perfect passive: will + have + been + V3. 'Will have written' → 'will have been written'. Both 'have' and 'been' are required.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to impersonal passive: People say that he is a genius.

options.option_text: He is said that he is a genius.
It is said that he is a genius.
It is being said that he is a genius.
He says he is a genius.

questions.explanation: Impersonal passive with 'people say': 'It is said that + original clause'. The tense of the embedded clause does not change in this structure.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change Passive to Active: Was the meal prepared by her?

options.option_text: Is the meal prepared by her?
Had she prepared the meal?
Did she prepare the meal?
She prepared the meal?

questions.explanation: Passive simple past question → Active: 'Did + subject + V1 + object?'. 'Was prepared' → 'Did she prepare'. The auxiliary 'Did' is used for simple past active questions.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: They were watching a movie.

options.option_text: A movie is being watched by them.
A movie was watched by them.
A movie was being watched by them.
A movie had been watched by them.

questions.explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were + being + V3. 'They were watching' → 'A movie was being watched by them'. 'Movie' is singular → 'was'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change Passive to Active: Is the work being done by him?

options.option_text: Was he doing the work?
Does he do the work?
Is he doing the work?
Will he do the work?

questions.explanation: Present continuous passive question → Active: 'Is + subject + V-ing + object?'. 'Is the work being done' → 'Is he doing the work?'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The news surprised everyone.

options.option_text: Everyone is surprised by the news.
Everyone was surprised by the news.
Everyone had been surprised by the news.
Everyone were surprised by the news.

questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was/were + V3. 'Everyone' is treated as singular → 'was'. 'Surprised' is V3.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice (WH question): Who broke this cup?

options.option_text: By whom this cup was broken?
By whom was this cup broken?
By whom has this cup been broken?
Who was this cup broken by?

questions.explanation: Passive WH question: 'By whom + was/were + subject + V3?' When 'who' is the subject in active, it becomes 'by whom' in passive, and the auxiliary is inverted.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: They will complete the building in two years.

options.option_text: The building will be completed by them in two years.
The building has been completed by them in two years.
The building would be completed by them in two years.
The building is to be completed by them in two years.

questions.explanation: Simple future passive: will + be + V3. 'Will complete' → 'will be completed'. Adverbial 'in two years' stays at the end.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The results pleased me.

options.option_text: I was pleased by the results.
I was pleased with the results.
I am pleased with the results.
I had been pleased with the results.

questions.explanation: Stative verbs like 'please', 'satisfy', 'interest' use 'with' not 'by' in passive. 'Pleased with the results' is the standard form. Tense: simple past → 'was pleased'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Active: She sent me an invitation. Which passive sentence retains 'I' as the grammatical subject?

options.option_text: I was sent an invitation by her.
An invitation was sent to me by her.
I sent an invitation.
An invitation was being sent to me by her.

questions.explanation: When the indirect object 'me' becomes the passive subject 'I', the form is: 'I was sent an invitation by her'. No 'to' before the direct object when indirect object is the new subject.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice (WH question): How did they manage the event?

options.option_text: How was the event managed by them?
How the event was managed by them?
How has the event been managed by them?
How did the event get managed by them?

questions.explanation: Passive WH question: 'How + was/were + subject + V3 + by + agent?' Auxiliary 'was' is inverted. 'Did they manage' (simple past) → 'was managed'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The artist had been painting the mural for years. Which passive form is conventionally acceptable for this sentence?

options.option_text: The mural had been being painted by the artist for years.
The mural was being painted by the artist for years.
The mural had been painted by the artist for years.
The mural was painted by the artist for years.

questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous passive ('had been being painted') is grammatically possible but stylistically awkward and uncommon in exams. The accepted conventional form is past perfect simple passive: 'had been painted'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: Can anyone solve this equation?

options.option_text: Can this equation solve by anyone?
Can this equation have been solved by anyone?
Can this equation be solved by anyone?
Could this equation be solved by anyone?

questions.explanation: Modal passive question: 'Can + subject + be + V3 + by + agent?' 'Can anyone solve' → 'Can this equation be solved by anyone?'. The modal 'can' is retained.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: She should complete the assignment today.

options.option_text: The assignment must be completed today by her.
The assignment should be completed today by her.
The assignment should have been completed today by her.
The assignment would be completed today by her.

questions.explanation: Modal passive: 'should + be + V3'. 'Should complete' → 'should be completed'. The modal 'should' is retained exactly.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The manager signed the document yesterday.

options.option_text: The document is signed by the manager yesterday.
The document had been signed by the manager yesterday.
The document was signed by the manager yesterday.
The document was being signed by the manager yesterday.

questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was + V3. 'Signed' is V3. 'Yesterday' (adverb of time) stays at the end.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change Passive to Active: He was seen crossing the road.

options.option_text: Someone saw him cross the road.
People see him crossing the road.
He was crossing the road.
People saw him crossing the road.

questions.explanation: Passive of perception verb + V-ing: 'He was seen crossing' → 'People/Someone saw him crossing'. The -ing participle is retained. Agent = 'People'. Tense: 'was seen' → 'saw' (simple past).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice (personal passive): It is alleged that he took bribes.

options.option_text: He is alleged that he took bribes.
He is being alleged to take bribes.
He is alleged to have taken bribes.
He is alleged to take bribes.

questions.explanation: Impersonal → personal passive: 'It is alleged that he took bribes' → 'He is alleged to have taken bribes'. The past tense in the 'that' clause becomes 'to have + V3' (perfect infinitive).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: They made him sign the agreement.

options.option_text: He was made sign the agreement by them.
He was made to sign the agreement.
He was made to sign the agreement by them.
He is made to sign the agreement by them.

questions.explanation: Causative passive: 'made + object + bare infinitive' → 'object + was made + to + infinitive'. The bare infinitive 'sign' acquires 'to' in the passive. By-phrase 'by them' is retained.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to personal passive: People believe that he committed the crime.

options.option_text: He is believed to commit the crime.
He is believed to have committed the crime.
It is believed that he commits the crime.
He is believed that he committed the crime.

questions.explanation: Personal passive: 'He is believed to have + V3' — the past tense 'committed' becomes 'to have committed' (perfect infinitive) to show the event preceded the belief.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Active: The committee awarded him the gold medal. Which passive form correctly uses the DIRECT object ('gold medal') as the new subject?

options.option_text: He was awarded the gold medal by the committee.
The gold medal was awarded him by the committee.
The gold medal was awarded to him by the committee.
Him was awarded the gold medal by the committee.

questions.explanation: When the direct object 'gold medal' becomes the passive subject, 'to' is placed before the indirect object: 'The gold medal was awarded to him by the committee'. Without 'to', the sentence is ungrammatical.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Identify the INCORRECT passive sentence:

options.option_text: She is known to be honest.
The work was got done by him.
He was resembled by his father.
The door was found open.

questions.explanation: 'Resemble' is a stative verb expressing a natural relationship — it cannot form a passive. 'He was resembled by his father' is incorrect. Other options are grammatically valid passives.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The fire had destroyed the entire village.

options.option_text: The entire village was destroyed by the fire.
The entire village had been destroyed by the fire.
The entire village has been destroyed by the fire.
The entire village had being destroyed by the fire.

questions.explanation: Past perfect passive: had + been + V3. 'Had destroyed' → 'had been destroyed'. 'Been' is mandatory between 'had' and the past participle.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: Somebody is following us.

options.option_text: We are followed by somebody.
We were being followed by somebody.
We are being followed.
We are being followed by somebody.

questions.explanation: Present continuous passive: are/is + being + V3. 'Somebody is following us' → 'We are being followed by somebody'. 'Somebody' as by-agent is retained (known agent).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Active: He was too weak to lift the box. Which is the best passive equivalent?

options.option_text: The box was too heavy for him to lift.
The box was too heavy to lift by him.
The box was too heavy to be lifted by him.
The box was too heavy to have been lifted by him.

questions.explanation: Passive infinitive form: 'to be + V3'. 'Too weak to lift' → 'too heavy to be lifted by him'. Option A is an active infinitive form (though commonly used); C is the strict passive infinitive form tested in exams.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: The teacher made the student rewrite the essay.

options.option_text: The student was made rewrite the essay by the teacher.
The essay was made to be rewritten by the student.
The student was made to rewrite the essay by the teacher.
The student is made to rewrite the essay by the teacher.

questions.explanation: Causative passive: 'made + bare infinitive' → 'was made + to + infinitive'. The student is the object of 'made', so 'the student' becomes the passive subject. Tense: simple past → 'was made'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: It is time to clean the room.

options.option_text: It is time to be cleaned the room.
It is time for the room to be cleaned.
It is time that the room is cleaned.
It is time the room should be cleaned.

questions.explanation: Passive infinitive: 'It is time for + noun + to be + V3'. 'It is time to clean the room' → 'It is time for the room to be cleaned'. The subject of the infinitive is introduced by 'for'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Active: She will have submitted the report. Which is the correct future perfect passive?

options.option_text: The report will be submitted by her.
The report will have submitted by her.
The report will have been submitted by her.
The report would have been submitted by her.

questions.explanation: Future perfect passive: will + have + been + V3. 'Will have submitted' → 'will have been submitted'. Both 'have' and 'been' are required between 'will' and the past participle.
questions.subject: English
